registration.custody: Selected numeric labels remain evaluator-side. File paths and separate on-disk locations restrict intended data flow. Both roles run under a shared administrative identity, and public timings can be independently found. No cryptographic isolation or prospective observation claim.
registration.event_binding: Use each source's observation date/epoch identity or independently published prior ephemeris for assignment before scoring. The blind manifest uses broad calendar windows, source filename/sector, planet and epoch metadata where publicly available, and SHA-256 for NASA bytes. Never derive its anchors from precise reference times. UTC civil-date hint to BJD_TDB search span is [date-JD minus 0.5 days, date-JD plus 1.5 days], and is intentionally broad.
physical_selection: Search public ExoFOP, ExoClock and the CHEOPS archive and literature for physically non-TESS, planet-attributed observations dated 2024-01-01 or later. Use all qualifying public measured timing rows with verifiable source bytes, declared BJD_TDB, and a documented uncertainty, provided eligible NASA TESS sampling overlaps the observed transit. Scope may fall back to earlier observations if recent physically independent rows cannot be obtained.

For the archival fallback use every ground-only published TOI-216 timing row with a reported uncertainty, BJD_TDB, and eligible NASA TESS observations covering the corresponding date. A timing solution that includes same-event TESS photons is ineligible as physically independent. Preserve uniquely sourced non-overlap rows for the independent-observation record and do not score them as matched windows.

Multiple ground exposures from one astronomical event or duplicate catalogue representations constitute one event. Use the source team's joint ground-only estimate where published. Otherwise retain all alternate estimates but choose the one with smallest reported one-sigma uncertainty as the primary event estimate, with stable source ID tiebreak.
registration.previous_use: Exclude every TOI-216 event identity and date window in frontier-lab/publication/cascade/RESULTS.json; prefer entirely unused FITS sectors. Use no previous numerical result to label or select a new row.
temporal_selection: Acquire public NASA SPOC target 2-minute light curves by TIC identity and dated archive records. Prefer sectors starting after 2023-12-31 and retain such newer products separately even if usable external evaluator timings are not found.

If published same-instrument evaluator rows after 2023 are unavailable, use securely attributable published ExoClock TESS rows from previously unused sectors from 2023. Retain every qualifying matched event on those products and clearly describe the reference's reuse of TESS photons.

No fit, observation depth, fitted uncertainty, numerical residual or scorer outcome may choose, replace or reject an event. Known coverage or provenance conflicts are reasons to mark an event ineligible or unscored rather than drop its record.
registration.timestamp_note: Registration written before extracting selected numeric source rows and before fits. Initial archive discovery exposed dates, bibliography, broad ephemerides and ExoClock TESS O-C snippets, so temporal results remain retrospective. Prior repository results were inspected solely to establish exclusions.

timing_scoring.concordance: Absolute error at most the larger of 120 seconds or three directional reference standard deviations. Positive error uses the upper uncertainty and negative error uses the lower. Report median absolute error using all measured matched events and count abstentions separately.
timing_scoring.coverage: Report whether a provided 90% interval contains the reference point, separately from agreement. Retain actual calibration denominators. Give a reference-uncertainty caveat for interval coverage. Avoid collapsing physical and same-photon rows in any accuracy claim.
timing_scoring.eligible: A prediction must identify a preassigned event and supply a finite BJD_TDB midtime. Keep all eligible cross-matched events in the denominator, including abstentions. Unlabeled events are not scored. Use fixed predictions and interval bytes hashed before evaluator labels are presented to the fitter.

source_adjudication.source_research:
# TOI-216 confirmation sources

The archive search produced two earlier cross-telescope timing comparisons, five 2023 TESS-to-TESS timing comparisons and nine 2024–2025 TESS sectors without an admissible numerical reference. This is retrospective evaluation. The source and fitting roles used separate files under one administrative identity. Public timings remain independently discoverable.

## NASA TESS

TIC 55652896 identifies TOI-216. Candidate fits use only the 20 two-minute NASA SPOC `LIGHTCURVE` FITS products bound to `BLIND.json`. Each file opens as TESS data with the expected sector, TIC, barycentric TDB time standard and product digest. The 20 files total 40,939,200 bytes. The manifest SHA-256 is `3f8919bc7f4d590fda15bc44d3b028c3e0d30a0ab24c46521a949383f4c954b6`. See the MAST sector scripts and the recorded product URLs in `NASA-DOWNLOADS.json` and `NASA-DOWNLOADS-LATE.json`. [MAST sector downloads](https://stdatu.stsci.edu/tess/bulk_downloads/bulk_downloads_ffi-tp-lc-dv.html)

| Manifest group | Sectors | Evaluator use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2018–2019 | 6, 7, 8, 12 | Cross-telescope overlaps in 6 and 8. At the ground reference times, sector 7 has no finite timestamps and sector 12 has 164 finite timestamps, all with quality 12288 and nonfinite PDCSAP flux. |
| 2023 | 61, 62, 63, 65, 66, 67, 68 | Five qualified same-photon checks. Four archive dates disagree with the registered two-day event window. Sectors 64 and 69 include previous Cascade measurements and were excluded entirely. |
| 2024–2025 | 87, 88, 89, 90, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98 | Nine later sectors cover December 2024 through January 2026. The public NASA photometry is suitable for exploratory fitting. Numerical timing accuracy for these sectors is unscored. |

## Ground photometry and independent reduction

Dawson et al. report separate TOI-216 c center parameters for ground light curves, with transit-shape parameters informed by their larger analysis. The selected ground exposures and space exposures originate from different telescopes. The independent evaluator reduction uses the original differential ground flux columns and avoids any TESS photometry, timing comparison, fitted ground columns or ephemeris anchor. Reference centers were available to the data custodian and do not enter the independent fit. [Dawson et al., The Astronomical Journal, Table 2](https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/abd8d0)

| Ground observation | Independent data | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2018-12-16 LCOGT 1 m at SAAO, Sinistro, i′ | ExoFOP file 5821, 857,851 bytes, SHA-256 `10510488e493c3e931013949e2c2d0f41a6aa54162a7be77fc13fa198da0ce01` | Observer RunB omits 29 likely saturated frames. 302 rows, 39 s median exposure. [Photometry](https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/get_file.php?id=5821) |
| 2019-02-24 El Sauce 0.36 m, SBIG STT-1603-3, R₍C₎ | ExoFOP file 10172, 2,110,833 bytes, SHA-256 `e25edc18b7a2dc8f52eebacac28367e6f6d9b14a357a5468fb5ec5b829deb088` | The target file name uses the prior night’s date. 514 rows, 30 s median exposure. [Photometry](https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/get_file.php?id=10172) |

The reduction uses AstroImageJ mid-exposure BJD_TDB, `rel_flux_T1`, `rel_flux_err_T1`, exposure duration and airmass. A limb-darkened occultation profile is integrated over each exposure for each model fit. Conditional errors include a residual-scale and 10-minute binning correction and the largest midpoint shift among the four model assumptions. These errors describe the observed model sensitivity and have no validated coverage level. [AstroImageJ user guide](https://astroimagej.com/guides/aij/) [ExoFOP DOI](https://doi.org/10.26134/ExoFOP5)

| Ground observation | Ground-only midtime, BJD_TDB | Conditional timing scale | Difference from Dawson Table 2 | Sample counts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| LCOGT | 2458469.47812369 | 65.30 s | +2.05 s | 80 before, 21 ingress, 167 in transit, 27 egress, 7 after |
| El Sauce | 2458538.58847767 | 1,617.48 s | −459.85 s | 435 in transit, 65 egress, 14 after |

The LCOGT visit spans 2018-12-16 18:52 through 2018-12-17 02:20 UTC. Its median quoted flux error is 0.595 ppt and the BJD_TDB–JD_UTC column difference is 95.13–95.47 s, which includes the barycentric light-time term. Its independent center agrees with the literal Dawson value and is 67.07 s earlier than the standardized ExoClock value. That difference supports treating the literal paper value as already TDB for this row. ExoClock assumes UTC when a publication omits the scale. [ExoClock time conversion policy](https://www.exoclock.space/database/planets)

The El Sauce visit spans 00:06–05:08 UTC on 2019-02-24. Its median quoted flux error is 2.972 ppt and the BJD_TDB–JD_UTC column difference is 22.29–22.55 s. Its missing ingress and pre-transit baseline limit precision. The chosen model has 599.18 s nominal white timing uncertainty and the tested models span 1,617.48 s from the primary center. Dawson’s reported El Sauce error is 0.0015 day, while ExoClock transcribes 0.015 day. The primary literature reference ledger uses the original paper’s uncertainty and records the catalogue’s UTC-assumed centre separately from the raw ground-only fit.

The frozen reference archive `by_planet/TOI-216.01.txt` and `by_planet/TOI-216.02.txt` are from ExoClock, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/WPJTN, 983,058 bytes, SHA-256 `0c17105ad6a7b4f50281c15f1ed61170163f008f00451c30bb25e39e83ef80e8`. The evaluator manifest retains 11 published ground timings, marks the two with quality-zero TESS transit cadence as eligible, and retains each uncertain or unavailable match as an unscored row. It uses a fixed acceptance rule of the larger of 120 seconds or three quoted reference standard deviations and reports any interval coverage separately. [ExoClock release](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/WPJTN)

## Reproduction

The fitter consumes `BLIND.json` only. The independent evaluator evidence is `evaluator/LABELS.json` and `evaluator/GROUND-ONLY.json`. The date, bounds and scoring criteria are in `REGISTRATION.json`, `PHYSICAL-INDEX.json` and `evaluator/GROUND-ONLY-REGISTRATION.json`. Ground comparisons to the literature are in `evaluator/GROUND-COMPARISON.json`.

```bash
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python evaluator/fit_ground.py --output evaluator/GROUND-ONLY-REPLAY.json
cmp evaluator/GROUND-ONLY.json evaluator/GROUND-ONLY-REPLAY.json
```
